.................................................................. 83 2 Executive Summary This report presents the findings from Task 7 of the project, which focused on improving the performance and reliability of wave energy converters (WECs) under real-world conditions, particularly in the presence of marine growth (biofouling) and system faults. The work was conducted using the RM3 point absorber WEC model, a marine current turbine based on the SHARKS project model, and the WEC-Sim simulation platform, and it included both modeling and control system development. Marine growth, such as barnacles and mussels, accumulates on submerged surfaces and alters the hydrodynamic properties of marine energy systems. For point absorber WECs, the research developed a drag coefficient model relating surface roughness from hard biofouling (mussels, barnacles) to hydrodynamic losses. The model adapts experimental data for perpendicular flow to the axial flow conditions relevant for heaving devices. WEC-Sim simulations of the RM3 device swept wave heights from 1-4 m, periods from 4-16 s, and biofouling protrusion from 0 to 0.1 m. At H=2m and resonant period (12s), heavy biofouling reduced PTO power by 15% while decreasing peak velocity and displacement by approximately 10%. Optimal PTO damping was found to decrease with increasing biofouling, but re-tuning control recovered only about 6% of lost power—demonstrating that biofouling effects are largely irreducible through damping control alone. Notably, the greatest performance sensitivity occurs with initial biofouling onset rather than continued growth. For hydrokinetic turbines, a reinforcement learning approach was developed to maximize energy generation as biofouling progressively degrades performance. A SARSA algorithm with Gaussian radial basis function approximation learns optimal damping coefficients as turbine dynamics change over time. Biofouling effects were modeled as shifts in the power coefficient curve, decreasing both optimal tip- speed ratio and maximum Cp based on experimental data.
